d: Jim learns that his neighbor (Julie Newmar) has written a series of children's books, modeling a grumpy old man on him.
After Jim makes a neighbor cry with a blunt remark at his backyard barbecue, Jim decides to reform and become the model of polite diplomacy.
Jim suspects that the father (Joseph Bologna) of one of Ruby and Gracie's classmates is his own real father, who abandoned him as a child.
Cheryl urges Jim to behave on St. Patrick's Day and forgo his annual law-bending "Green Man" routine so she can assure herself an appointment to the church committee.
Andy starts to play chess with Ryan on a regular basis, and jealous Jim assumes Andy is no longer his best friend.
Jim advises Ryan (Mitch Rouse) on how to deal with fluctuating hormones when he announces that Dana is expecting.
Jim teaches Kyle to throw the perfect punch to defend himself against the school bully, but Kyle gets suspended for repeatedly hitting the other child.
As a talk-show guest, Jim angers Cheryl by expressing the view that men should not let women feminize them.
Jim must pay for an expensive operation to keep the family's pet guinea pig alive.
Jim and Cheryl try to celebrate their 15th anniversary in an Indiana motel but must drive back to Chicago when Dana thinks she is in labor.
Jim takes over housekeeping duties to give Cheryl time to grieve when her favorite uncle dies, but begins to suspect Cheryl is faking her grief to get him to do more housework.
Raging Jim accidentally backs into a police car while chasing a guy and chooses anger-management classes instead of paying the fine.
Jim, Ryan and Andy learn that Cheryl and Dana have appeared in a "Chicks Gone Wild" video.
While Dana is in premature labor, Ryan is in a war-torn country, delivering a celebrity's baby.
Dana and Cheryl hesitantly entrust Ryan and Jim to watch the kids and baby Tanner while they have a girls night out.
